how_to_run: Run each prompt in a fresh session with the skill available. Grade every 'must' item pass/fail; the case passes only if all 'must' items pass. 'must_not' items are automatic fails.

cases.prompt: Dos fábricas de cemento compiten en cantidades. Demanda P = 100 - Q. Costos marginales 10 y 20. ¿Cuánto produce cada una y qué pasa si la segunda baja su costo a 15?
must: Writes the five pieces (players, actions, timing, information, payoffs)
Equilibrium q1 = 33.3, q2 = 23.3 obtained with continuous_br.py (not by hand only)
Reports verification (no profitable deviation) and the grid check
Comparative statics: q2 rises by 3.33 and q1 falls by 1.67 when c2 falls by 5
States quantities are strategic substitutes and explains it in plain words
Explains why the equilibrium is stable using deviation logic

cases.prompt: Dos estaciones de servicio enfrentadas venden nafta idéntica, costo $1000 el litro. ¿A qué precio terminan? ¿Cambia algo que los precios sean en pesos enteros?
must: Identifies homogeneous Bertrand: continuous equilibrium p = c
Notes that with discrete prices there is also an equilibrium at c + 1 (grid check shows both)
Referee: repeated interaction / price transparency make tacit collusion plausible (Bertrand paradox resolution); capacity, location differentiation
Gives critical discount factor logic for collusion (delta >= 1/2 for duopoly grim trigger)

cases.prompt: Dos empresas compiten en un concurso donde ambas pagan su inversión gane o pierda; el premio vale 1 millón para A y 800 mil para B. ¿Cuánto invierte cada una?
must: Recognizes an all-pay contest with no pure equilibrium
Uses mixed_continuous.py
Reports: both mix on [0, 800k]; B places ~20% mass at zero; A's expected payoff ≈ 200k, B's ≈ 0
Explains indifference: every bid in the support gives the same expected payoff
Counterintuitive point: total expected spending is large relative to the prize (rent dissipation)

cases.prompt: Soy el único supermercado de un pueblo. Si entra una cadena, puedo hacer guerra de precios (yo gano 1, ellos pierden 2) o acomodarme (yo 4, ellos 3). Si no entran gano 9. ¿Amenazo con guerra de precios?
must: Uses extensive_form.py; SPE = Enter, Accommodate
Flags the price-war threat as not credible and explains why
Discusses what would make it credible: commitment (capacity, contracts, reputation in multiple markets)
Gives a threshold: e.g. the investment/commitment that makes fighting optimal

cases.prompt: Tengo una cadena de supermercados medianos en CABA y quiero abrir uno en Villa Crespo. Tengo 4 locales candidatos (te paso coordenadas y alquileres). ¿Cuál elijo? Me preocupa que Carrefour también esté buscando en la zona.
must: Asks for (or labels as assumptions) margin, spend per capita, rents, own store locations
Mentions SEPA / census radios as data sources and uses competitors_osm.py
Detects that OSM buildings are incomplete in CABA and uses census or the street proxy, saying so
Runs huff.py with network distance, beta sweep and cannibalization
Runs location_game.py and contrasts naive vs strategic choice
Flags near ties and edge effects when present
Produces a map (map.py) with annotation
Gives a threshold that flips the recommendation (rent difference or rival move)
Game card with executive / intuitive / formal levels
must_not: Picks a winner when the top two differ by < 5% without saying it is a tie

cases.prompt: ¿Por qué las heladerías se juntan en la misma cuadra y los supermercados se separan?
must: Hotelling: fixed prices → clustering; price competition with quadratic costs → maximum differentiation
Agglomeration from consumer search vs convenience goods
Short answer: does NOT run the map pipeline
One-sentence memorable intuition

cases.prompt: Explicale a mi socio, que no es economista, por qué conviene que el competidor sepa que ya firmamos el alquiler.
must: Story in two lines without jargon
Concept: commitment / first-mover advantage; observability is essential (a secret commitment is worth nothing)
Uses numbers (even illustrative, labeled)
No terms like 'subgame perfect' in the intuitive level

cases.prompt: Two ice-cream carts on a 1 km beach with fixed prices. Where do they stand? And if they can set prices freely and walking cost is quadratic?
must: Fixed prices: both at the median (hotelling.py location --stage fixed)
Price competition with quadratic costs: maximum differentiation at the ends; prices = t
Compares with social optimum (quartiles): too little vs too much differentiation
Tent diagram as the picture

cases.prompt: Three gas stations along a highway, regulated identical prices. Where do they locate?
must: Recognizes Eaton-Lipsey: no pure equilibrium with 3 firms
Shows it with hotelling.py (exhaustive grid proof)
Discusses what happens in practice: sequential entry, mixed strategies, other dimensions

cases.prompt: Voy a subastar una obra; creo que hay 4 compradores serios con valuaciones lognormales alrededor de USD 50k (sigma 0.5). Yo la valoro en 20k. ¿Qué reserva pongo? ¿Conviene más buscar otro comprador?
must: Uses auctions.py reserve with lognormal and v0
Reports Myerson reserve and that it does not depend on n
Bulow-Klemperer comparison with numbers
Mentions buyer's premium / estimates as context; English auction ≈ second price

cases.prompt: In a road tender, one incumbent has costs ~U[60,100] and two entrants ~U[70,120]. First-price sealed bid. What will they bid and is the auction efficient? Should the agency give entrants a bidding credit?
must: Uses auctions.py numeric --procurement with three bidders
Reports bid functions, efficiency below 100%, expected spend vs second-price
Explains weak bidders bid more aggressively
Discusses bidding credits / preferences as a design tool with a quantified trade-off or a clear way to quantify it

cases.prompt: Tengo un CSV de licitaciones con todas las ofertas. ¿Cómo sé si los márgenes son competitivos o hay colusión?
must: Normalizes bids by an estimate/budget before GPV
Runs auctions.py gpv by number of bidders
Reads markups vs n and monotonicity as red flags, not proof
Lists screens (rotation, cover bids) and legal caveat

cases.prompt: I have a job offer for 90k; my current job pays 80k; the new employer would pay up to maybe 110k (my guess: normal with mean 105k, sd 10k). What should I ask for?
must: Uses bargaining.py offer with the reservation = 80k-equivalent BATNA and the employer's max as distribution
Gives an ask with acceptance probability and expected gain
Explains outside option principle (the current job only matters if it beats the bargaining share)
Mentions improving the BATNA (another offer) as the main lever

cases.prompt: Negociación con un proveedor: precio, plazo de pago, volumen mínimo y exclusividad. ¿Cómo armo la propuesta?
must: Builds an issues JSON with each side's priorities (asks or assumes, labeled)
Runs bargaining.py issues
Shows that splitting each issue is inefficient and proposes logrolling
States BATNAs and the ZOPA

cases.prompt: Where should I open a pharmacy in Valencia, Spain? Here are 3 candidate addresses.
must: Uses Spanish sources (INE secciones censales + renta, regulated pharmacy distances/ratios rules in Spain as legal constraint)
Competitors from OSM and Overture
Does not assume Argentine sources or currency

cases.prompt: Two supermarket chains with 30% and 25% of a regional market want to merge; the others have 20, 15 and 10. Survey says 30% of chain A's customers would switch to B. Margins around 25%. Will the authority object and how much would prices rise?
must: merger.py hhi with US/EU/UK readings (ΔHHI 1500)
merger.py upp with stated or labeled diversion/margins; GUPPI and CMCR
Mentions local market definition (catchments) - links to location module
Efficiency claims vs CMCR as the threshold

cases.prompt: I have prices and market shares of beers across 300 cities. How price-sensitive is demand?
must: merger.py demand with outside share defined by market size
Explains price endogeneity and proposes instruments (Hausman, cost shifters, BLP)
Reports OLS vs 2SLS and elasticities; validates implied margins

cases.prompt: En mi ciudad las 4 estaciones de servicio cambian el precio el mismo día. ¿Es colusión?
must: collusion.py sustain (few firms, daily interaction, public prices → easy to sustain)
collusion.py prices on a station-level panel (suggests the country's open fuel/price data)
Distinguishes Edgeworth cycles / common cost shocks from coordination
States that screens are red flags, not proof; legal context

cases.prompt: Here's a CSV of 5 years of municipal road tenders with all bids. Find anything suspicious.
must: collusion.py bids with estimate if available
auctions.py gpv markups vs n
Reports rotation groups, cover-bid tenders, never-winning bidders
Innocent explanations and next steps (before/after events, Porter-Zona)

cases.prompt: En una especie de pájaros, pelear por un territorio vale 2 y una herida cuesta 4. ¿Qué proporción de agresivos esperás?
must: evolutionary.py ess --hawk-dove 2,4 → mixed ESS 50% hawks (V/C)
Explains stability as self-correcting frequencies
Phase line plot
Sensitivity: if C < V all hawks

cases.prompt: Why might a whole industry stick with an inferior technical standard even when a better one exists?
must: Coordination game with two ESS
Risk dominance vs payoff dominance; basins (dynamics) and stochastic selection (moran / KMR)
Real examples and what could tip the market (subsidies, coalitions of early adopters)

cases.prompt: A new mutation gives a 1% advantage in heterozygotes in a population of 500 individuals. What's the chance it spreads?
must: genetics with Kimura: ≈ 2s ≈ 2% vs neutral 0.1%
Wright-Fisher simulation agreeing
Explains most beneficial mutations are lost to drift early

cases.prompt: ¿Cómo puede sobrevivir la cooperación si los que se aprovechan siempre ganan más?
must: PD is not cooperative in well-mixed populations (ess)
At least three mechanisms (kin, reciprocity, reputation, spatial) with their thresholds
spatial run showing clusters
